The pages below belong to the measurement models in the
[bmm](https://venpopov.com/bmm/) R package. Each one lets you move a model's parameters and watch the
predicted responses change, shows the task the model is written for, and, where the model has
something to say about it, what happens when the task changes while the parameters do not. Nothing
is installed and nothing is sent anywhere: the curves are computed in your browser.

## Categorical decision tasks

- [Memory Measurement Model (`m3`)](models/m3.qmd): a correct item, other list items, distractors and
  new lures compete for a response, in simple and complex span, under three choice rules. Candidate
  counts are part of the model.
- [Multinomial processing tree, span task (`mpt`)](models/mpt.qmd): recall as discrete states, with
  guessing rates set by the response set, and how it relates to the M3.

## Continuous reproduction tasks

- [Interference Measurement Model (`imm`)](models/imm.qmd): responses on a colour wheel drawn to the
  target, to the other items by their closeness to the cued location, and to noise. Set size and
  spacing are part of the model.
- [Two-parameter mixture model (`mixture2p`)](models/mixture2p.qmd): responses centred on the target,
  or guesses. No task setting enters the likelihood.
- [Three-parameter mixture model (`mixture3p`)](models/mixture3p.qmd): adds responses to the
  non-targets. Their colours and their number enter the density; from set size 2 on, more
  non-targets split the same weight.
- [Signal discrimination model (`sdm`)](models/sdm.qmd): one distribution with a memory strength and a
  precision, and no separate guessing parameter. No task setting enters the likelihood.

More pages follow in the order of [the roadmap](https://github.com/GidonFrischkorn/bmm-explorer/blob/main/dev/ROADMAP.md):
the signal detection family and the response-time models.

New here? Read [how to read a page](about.qmd) first.
